short: His reworking of Plato as a philosophy of ascent to the divine shaped both pagan and Christian thought.
full:
Born in Egypt around AD 205, Plotinus studied for eleven years under the Alexandrian teacher Ammonius Saccas before settling in Rome in 244, where he lectured until his death around 270. His philosophy, later called Neoplatonism, described reality as emanating in stages from a single transcendent source, the One, through Intellect and Soul down to the material world, with the philosophical life understood as a disciplined ascent back toward that source.

Plotinus wrote nothing himself until his final decade; his student Porphyry collected and edited the results as the Enneads after his death. The system gave late antique paganism its most sophisticated intellectual defence and, through Augustine and later Christian writers who read it as compatible with scripture, fed directly into medieval Christian theology, making Plotinus one of the most influential philosophers between Aristotle and Aquinas.
